name: Direct3D-V3 — mesh detail refiner from one image (MIT code + weights)
summary: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 model that turns a rough 3D mesh plus one reference image (ideally a normal map or clay render) into a finely detailed mesh. It runs diffusion directly on SDF voxel grids (512/1024/1536) with no VAE. Inference code and weights released Nov 19. Coarse-mesh and texture models are not released yet; for now the coarse mesh comes from another tool (e.g. Hunyuan3D-2.1, with its own license).

publisher.name: DreamTech / Nanjing University (Shuang Wu et al.)

access.notes: MIT on code and HF weights. Needs DINOv3 (gated on HF, Meta license) and BiRefNet. Optional helpers Hunyuan3D-2.1/UltraShape (Tencent community license) and Qwen-Image-2.1 (non-commercial) carry their own terms.

procedure: Clone https://github.com/DreamTechAI/Direct3D-V3 (Linux, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, CUDA 13.0, C++20 compiler)
Install requirements, FlashAttention 2 and the bundled voxelization/fill_holes extensions as in the README
Request access to DINOv3 ViT-H+ on Hugging Face; weights load from wushuang98/Direct3D-V3 by default
Prepare a coarse mesh (OBJ/GLB/PLY) aligned with your reference image, plus a normal map or white clay render of it
Run infer.py or app.py with --coarse-mesh and --image

verdict.why: MIT weights for high-detail mesh refinement is rare; strong results. Not end-to-end yet (bring your own coarse mesh), heavy CUDA setup and a gated DINOv3 dependency.

image.alt: Grey untextured meshes generated by Direct3D-V3: dragons, a cottage, mech, dwarves and a toad warrior on a grassy hill
